citation: O’Shaughnessy et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:3840–3847
design: Randomised phase III; gemcitabine/carboplatin served as control
population: Stage IV/locally recurrent TNBC; no more than two prior metastatic chemotherapy regimens
schedule: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC2 on Days1 and8 every21days, with or without investigational iniparib
interpretation: Neither coprimary endpoint met its prespecified significance criterion. These HRs estimate addition of iniparib; they are not the benefit of GC versus no chemotherapy or an alternative regimen.
limitations: Historical trial population and comparator; not a contemporary treatment-selection ranking.
No median survival or GC response estimate is imported from secondary reviews; full primary tables were inaccessible.
NCCP marks this indication unlicensed in Ireland; source requires local off-label consent/governance.
mechanism: Gemcitabine nucleotide metabolites inhibit DNA synthesis/ribonucleotide reductase; carboplatin creates DNA crosslinks. Combining them has a cytotoxic rationale, but molecular rationale alone does not prove superiority.

citation: Modi et al. Clin Breast Cancer 2005;6(1):55–60
population: Measurable metastatic breast cancer after2–4 prior chemotherapy regimens including anthracycline and taxane
schedule: Gemcitabine800mg/m² Days1,8,15 every28days until progression in the study

endpoints.endpoint: Partial tumour regression among response-evaluable patients

interpretation: Evidence of activity in heavily pretreated disease; no randomised survival benefit estimate.
limitations: Small sample and wide confidence interval.
Response-evaluable denominator is18, not all22 enrolled.
The NCCP treatment schedule specifies6–8cycles unless progression/toxicity; study duration until progression must not overwrite NCCP duration.
Do not infer that17% is an individual chance of benefit or a modern cross-trial comparison.
mechanism: Gemcitabine is a deoxycytidine analogue; activated metabolites inhibit DNA synthesis and ribonucleotide reductase. Separate from fluoropyrimidines: no CMF/5-FU DPD requirement is inherited.
